thread:
raj: Seeing steady GPU pool depletion in us-west1, ~40% capacity gone in last 10m, lots of cold-starts. Investigating.
status-bot: Alert: elevated GPU errors in us-west1 — auto-alert sent to oncall.
maria: Confirmed NIC flaps on a subset of hosts, kernel dmesg shows:
```
mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: link down
```
Isolating rack-3 nodes.
tim: Route affected: production/gpu-gen1. Initiating traffic-shift to us-central (weighting 0.7->0.3) and spinning up burst pool.
alex: Support: flagging high-priority Dedicated customers. Drafting status page text — ETA for public update?
naomi: 15m to publish, but need a clear ETA for full remediation to share with enterprise.
raj: Short-term mitigation: failover sessions to us-central possible; long-running KV sessions may restart. Net team working on fabric patch.
tim: Executing emergency route change: `rictl route set --region us-central --weight 0.6 --policy emergency` — running now.
maria: Starting firmware rollback test on host-03 in rack-3, will observe for 5m before proceeding.
status-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1031 - Networking - us-west1 GPU fabric - severity: high - assigned: infra.

tim: Observability: API 503s up ~10%, request queue latency +250ms for gpu-gen1. Scaling burst pool +15% to absorb surge.
raj: Update: rollback test on host-03 stable for 7m, proceeding rack-by-rack starting rack-3 -> rack-4. If no regressions, expect restoration in ~40-50m.
alex: I escalated to three enterprise customers; they're standing by with war rooms. I'll post updates every 15m.
naomi: GTM note: customers >$100k receive direct email and war room invites.
maria: Rack-3 patch complete, bringing nodes back into rotation gradually to avoid flapping.

raj: Current status: traffic shifted, degraded capacity being restored; monitoring closely. Tag me @raj for urgent escalations.
